title: The railroad record with Wells and Robert Pete Williams
summary: Maxey helped make a railroad work-song record with improvised tools, with Guitar Welch and Robert Pete Williams; talk about their whereabouts.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Did you ever drive spikes here on the red road? Line to try and come in here?

Well I didn't do it I seen the right smart of it did And of course I helped the boys Who put out a record of the railroad I hope them last year Put out a record of that Of course we well practiced it up Before we put it out And made a good hit out And made a good record out of it
How did you do that exactly? How did you make the record? You didn't have any railroad to work on did you?

Well we had little pieces Small railroad irons We had hammers We had pipes We had holes We had shovels And we just made a nice thing It went just like the rail Like we was right out there On the railroad track working And so we just carried a nice record out of it Right on down Well that was all made by me With Hogman Maxie Guitar Wells Robert Pete Williams So that made a Well us three made that record of it
